name: Zygopush

lead: Zygopush is a self-massage trend in looksmaxxing and face-yoga circles. The thumbs are placed beneath the cheekbones (the zygomatic bones) and pushed along them toward the ears, with the aim of lifting the cheekbones, hollowing the cheeks and sharpening the midface.

Practitioners describe it as a quick, free way to try to get a more sculpted look. No peer-reviewed studies have examined the technique, and health sites note that cheek shape depends mainly on bone structure and the amount of facial fat.

paras: Users describe using the thumbs with light to moderate pressure along the underside of the cheekbone, in repeated strokes toward the ears, usually as part of a face-massage or face-yoga routine. Some pair it with other facial massage, and results are usually judged by photos over weeks.

Gentle massage is generally considered low-risk, though heavy pressure can irritate skin. Some face-yoga practitioners have suggested that over-working the area could contribute to loss of volume under the eyes, a view from commercial sources rather than research.

chain: Thumb pressure along the underside of the cheekbone
angle.text: Practitioners say the massage lifts and defines the cheekbones and hollows the cheeks. Massage may temporarily move fluid and soft tissue, but its effect on bone or fat has not been studied.

lead: Zygopush, also written zygo pushing or zygopulling, is a facial-massage technique circulated on social media and in looksmaxxing forums. The thumbs press beneath the zygomatic bone, the cheekbone, and sweep toward the ears, in the belief that this can hollow the cheeks and make the cheekbones appear higher and more defined.

It sits within a wider family of cheek-sculpting methods such as buccal massage, face yoga and chewing exercises. Healthline describes cheek shape as depending on bone structure and facial fat, notes that exercises for hollow cheeks lack evidence, and lists buccal fat removal, cheek or jaw implants and makeup contouring as cosmetic options [1].

paras: The technique is described as placing the thumbs under the cheekbones and pushing or pulling toward the ears. It is shared mostly through short videos and forum posts, often under names like zygo pushing or zygopulling, and is related to buccal massage and face yoga.

Proponents say regular zygopushing makes cheekbones look higher and cheeks more hollow. Health sources describe cheek shape as determined largely by genetics, bone structure and facial fat, and state there is no evidence that cheek exercises are effective, while describing spot reduction as a myth [1].
